what_happened: On a multi-lane highway with a STRAIGHT and then RIGHT command, the policy's planned path (orange) bent left, away from the recorded path (green). The ego drifted left across the lane line into the next lane and its front corner hit actor 41, which was travelling alongside in that lane, at about 4.7 m/s.

On an open highway with no lead vehicle (the gap is null or 44–54 m and growing), the policy braked hard for no visible reason, from 23.7 to 6.9 m/s in 3 s, and fell about 9.5 m behind its recorded position. Actor 1, a replayed car coming up in the left lane, then merged across where the human-driven car had already passed and met the ego's front corner, which counts as a front collision.

On a straight multi-lane highway, the policy planned a drift to the left (orange path) while the recorded route stayed in lane. At 7.7 s, travelling about 5 m/s, the ego's front cut into vehicle 41, which was alongside in the left lane.

On a multi-lane highway with a STRAIGHT and then RIGHT command, the policy's planned path (orange) kept bending left of the route. The ego drifted left across the lane line and its front hit actor 41, which was travelling alongside in the adjacent left lane.

On an open highway with no lead within about 43 m, the ego braked hard for no clear reason (23.7 to 7.2 m/s) and drifted left toward the lane line. Actor 1, coming up from behind in the left lane, drew alongside, and the ego's front-left clipped it. Actor 1 was simply driving its recorded path.

After handoff, the ego braked hard on an open highway, slowing from 18 to 4.4 m/s even though the nearest vehicle ahead was 44–54 m away, and it drifted slightly left of its route. The recorded ego position kept moving ahead without it. Actor 28, which had been following in the ego's original lane and does not react to the ego, caught up and hit the ego's right side and rear quarter at 8.6 s. This is labeled `other` because the root cause is unprovoked phantom braking, not a missed brake or a turn.

The ego went straight on a busy multi-lane highway and hit the back of the blue pickup (actor 5) that was slowing in its lane. When the policy took over at 4.7s, the gap was already only 6.3 m and closing at about 6 m/s. The policy did brake, from 9.3 to 7.6 m/s in the 0.5 s before impact, but not hard enough. A rear contact also happened at some point, but the at-fault front collision began first.

On a straight multi-lane highway, the ego closed on slower lead car 48 in its lane during the pre-handoff replay (gap 18.6 m down to 4.8 m by handoff at 4.7 s, at about 7.7 m/s). After taking over, the policy braked only slightly (7.7 to 6.7 m/s) and hit 48's rear 0.5 s later, still almost on the recorded human path.

The ego was following a blue pickup (actor 5) in its lane on a multi-lane highway and closed from about 16 m to 6 m before the handoff at 4.7 s. In the 0.5 s after taking over, the policy slowed only from 9.3 to 7.6 m/s and rear-ended the pickup at 5.2 s (a front collision).

The ego was going straight and closing on the blue pickup (actor 5) ahead in its lane. It was at 9.3 m/s with a 6.3 m gap when the policy took over at 4.7 s, and it front-ended the pickup 0.5 s later at 7.6 m/s. Stopping in time from handoff would have taken about 7 m/s² of braking, so the crash was mostly set up before the policy had control, although the policy braked only moderately (about 3.4 m/s²).

The policy took over at 4.7 s already 4.8 m behind the slower white sedan (actor 48) in its lane, closing at about 4–5 m/s, which is roughly 1 s to impact. It slowed only from 7.7 to 6.7 m/s and planned a swerve left toward actor 5 instead of braking hard, and its front hit 48 at 5.2 s (the ego was also rear-ended at some point).

The ego was going straight on a busy freeway and closing on slower lead vehicle 48 in its lane: the gap fell from 18.6 m to 4.8 m by handoff at 4.7 s. In its 0.5 s of control the policy braked only mildly (7.7 to 6.7 m/s) and planned a late swerve left instead of braking hard, so it hit the back of 48 at 5.2 s. The rear contact came after that front collision.

In slow freeway traffic, the policy took over at 4.7 s about 6.8 m behind a slower car in its lane (actor 12), with the gap closing quickly. It braked only moderately (6.0 to 4.4 m/s) and started a late nudge to the left instead of stopping, so its front hit actor 12's rear at 5.7 s. The car behind (rear_ended) only touched the ego after that.

In straight highway traffic, the ego was closing on slower lead car 12 in its lane: the gap fell from 14.6 m to 5.5 m during the replayed part of the run. The policy took over at 4.7 s with a gap of 5.5 m and about 3 m/s closing speed, slowed only from 6.0 to 5.4 m/s, and hit car 12's rear 0.5 s later at 5.2 s, while its planned path was starting to veer left.
